items.headline: GitHub Copilot Best Practices from High-Performing Teams
items.summary: High-performing development teams using GitHub Copilot standardize context-rich prompting through descriptive function names, intent comments, and pinned files rather than relying on default completions. Teams decompose work into small reviewable steps and use fast models for inline completions, mid-tier reasoning models for multi-file refactors, and frontier models only for architectural planning. Teams in 2026 often combine Cursor or VS Code plus Copilot for daily coding with Claude Code for long agentic sessions like cross-cutting refactors.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's internal development teams use GitHub Copilot and Claude extensively. This best-practice guide can be shared in the next all-hands to improve team velocity on client delivery projects. The context-rich prompting pattern and model-tier selection strategy are directly applicable to our Salesforce implementation teams building Agentforce agents and our Microsoft Fabric data engineering practice. Recommend scheduling a 30-minute workshop with the delivery leads this quarter.

items.headline: Madison Square Garden breach exposed 26 million visitor records including facial recognition data
items.summary: Madison Square Garden suffered a data breach in June 2026 exposing 26 million visitor records including contact information and facial recognition data. The incident is part of a broader trend where AI-enabled attacks rose 89% this year, with autonomous agents involved in 1 in 8 AI breaches. Healthcare provider Xsolis also suffered a phishing breach compromising 1.4 million patient records, and London Hydro reported unauthorized access on June 20. The Cloud Security Alliance found 80% of organizations suffered incidents from known vulnerabilities with only 9% patching critical flaws within 24 hours.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's SOC 2 certification and HIPAA-compliant services differentiate us in exactly this threat landscape. Financial services and healthcare clients are our two largest verticals and face the tightest AI security requirements. Use this as a door-opener for our AI governance advisory practice with prospects currently attempting AI without proper security frameworks.

items.headline: AI Agent Standards Initiative for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
items.summary: NIST announced the AI Agent Standards Initiative in February 2026 to ensure AI agents capable of autonomous actions are adopted with confidence, function securely, and interoperate across the digital ecosystem. This follows NIST releasing a Cybersecurity Framework Profile for AI in December 2025 and an April 2026 concept note for Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructure. The initiative addresses the shift from foundational AI guidance to operational, sector-specific implementation frameworks for energy, healthcare, transportation, and other critical infrastructure.
